subject: MSA + Order Form: SLO tiering, response ladders, and maintenance blackout carveouts
messages: From: Vivek Kulkarni To: Elena Soto Cc: Marissa Cole Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2025 10:12:00 -0700 Subject: MSA + Order Form: SLO tiering, response ladders, and maintenance blackout carveouts Hi Elena — Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion I've attached a draft SLO matrix and a short redline of the Order Form sections that reference uptime and credits (SLO_matrix_v3.xlsx, BlueHarbor_MSA_redline.docx). High-level ask from our side: can you confirm whether the following are acceptable to Blue Harbor before we route to Legal for final redlines? - Tier A (critical production): 99.95% monthly uptime; P1 response target 1 hour (acknowledge) / 4 hours (initial mitigation) - Tier B (non-critical): 99.5% uptime; P2 response 4 hours / 24 hours - Quarterly maintenance blackout carveout: up to 8 hours per quarter per region; Greater maintenance to be scheduled as a negotiated outage with 30 days' notice - Service credit cap at 15% of monthly invoice per month; staircase credits by outage magnitude (matrix in sheet) If Blue Harbor needs tighter uptime or different credit caps, call that out and we can propose mitigations (runbook commitments, canary routing, fallback model variant) to reduce the credit exposure. Next steps: if you can reply with high-level accept/decline items today, I'll pull Legal (cc: Hannah) and Sales Ops (Marissa) into a short redline session tomorrow. Thanks, Vivek Vivek Kulkarni Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference (v) 415-555-0128 From: Elena Soto To: Vivek Kulkarni Cc: Tom Nguyen , Procurement Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -07:00 Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: SLO tiering, response ladders, and maintenance blackout carveouts Vivek — Appreciate the summary and the files. Quick reactions from the engineering and procurement side: - Uptime target: 99.95% for Tier A feels low for our payments flow; we need to target 99.99% for Tier A. - Credit cap: 15% monthly cap is higher than our policy allows; procurement prefers 10% with a cumulative annual cap. - Maintenance: the 8-hour quarterly allowance is reasonable, but we need a hard ‘no-maintenance’ window for our reconciliation day (first Sunday of the month, 02:00–06:00 local). Any maintenance that would touch that window must be blocked unless we give explicit waiver. - Response ladder: the ack/mitigation split looks fine; we need SLAs around root-cause timelines (RCA within 72 hours for P1s). If Redwood can commit to an automated fallback and documented runbook that reduces risk of broad outages, procurement may be more flexible on uptime. Can Marissa and Hannah coordinate with our legal/ops on exact redlines? Elena Elena Soto Director of Infrastructure | Blue Harbor Inc. elena.soto@blueharbor.com From: Marissa Cole To: Elena Soto Cc: Vivek Kulkarni , Hannah Schmitt Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2025 13:22:00 -07:00 Subject: Fwd: MSA + Order Form: SLO tiering, response ladders, and maintenance blackout carveouts Forwarding Elena's notes into Legal — Team — forwarding Blue Harbor's initial asks. Two items I think we can propose as compromises: 1) Offer a 99.99% uptime commitment for Tier A but tie it to a narrower incident definition and an automated fallback guarantee (we supply model-fallback + degraded-capacity mode). 2) Reduce the credit cap to 12% monthly with an annual cumulative floor; escalate to 15% only if outages are caused by unmitigated platform defects per runbook. Hannah, can you propose language for the Order Form that preserves both parties' ability to operationally mitigate while keeping credit exposure predictable? Marissa Sr. Account Exec | Redwood Inference From: Hannah Schmitt To: Marissa Cole , Vivek Kulkarni Cc: Elena Soto Date: Tue, 09 Sep 2025 09:18:00 -07:00 Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: SLO tiering, response ladders, and maintenance blackout carveouts Marissa / Vivek / Elena — Thanks for the context. I've reviewed the attached redline and sketched alternate Order Form language. Key legal proposals below: - SLO Definitions: define availability as "successful token-level responses excluding scheduled maintenance and customer-caused outages". Add explicit measurement window (UTC calendar month) and monitoring sources (primary: Redwood metrics; customer may request a mutually agreed audit once per year). - Uptime & Credits: offer 99.99% for Tier A with a stepped credit schedule: * >=99.95% but <99.99% = 5% credit * >=99.9% but <99.95% = 10% credit * <99.9% = 20% credit Monthly credit cap at 12%; annual cumulative cap at 25% (to address Blue Harbor's risk tolerance). - Response Ladder: require acknowledgement times and initial mitigation windows in the Order Form; require RCA for P1 within 72 hours with a remediation plan within 10 business days. Include a clause that if customer does not cooperate with incident reproduction requests, credits may be adjusted. - Maintenance carveouts: accept customer blackout window request for first Sunday 02:00–06:00 local. Define scheduled maintenance process: 30 days' notice for non-emergency maintenance; emergency maintenance allowed with as-notified notice and reasonable attempt to avoid blackout windows. Limit scheduled maintenance to 24 hours per year outside the quarterly 8-hour buckets unless mutually agreed. - Operational mitigations: add an appendix describing fallback behavior (automated model variant routing) and runbook commitments; these will be non-contractual operational commitments initially but can be elevated to binding SLO-reduction levers after mutual testing. I'll produce tracked-changes language and share within this thread by end of day. If Blue Harbor agrees to the stepped credit schedule and the 12% cap, we can close Order Form language and proceed to DocuSign. Hannah Schmitt Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference From: Jonas Weber To: Vivek Kulkarni , Marissa Cole Cc: Elena Soto , Hannah Schmitt Date: Tue, 09 Sep 2025 11:45:00 -07:00 Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: SLO tiering, response ladders, and maintenance blackout carveouts Quick ops input on the fallback/runbook side — We can deliver an automated fallback that reduces latency and lowers blast radius in 3 phases: 1) Prefix/KV cache priming for payments endpoints to reduce cold-starts (low effort). 2) Canary routing to a lighter-weight quantized variant during detected degradation (medium effort; requires model pinning in Order Form). 3) Region-level graceful degradation with routing to a read-only replica for non-critical reads (higher effort). If Blue Harbor accepts a documented 30-day testing window as part of Go-Live, we'll commit to enabling phase 1 immediately and phase 2/3 per the rollout plan. This operational proof will materially reduce the chance of hitting credit thresholds. Jonas Sr. Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference From: Vivek Kulkarni To: Elena Soto , Tom Nguyen Cc: Marissa Cole , Hannah Schmitt , Jonas Weber Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 16:45:00 -07:00 Subject: Summary & next steps — SLOs, credits, maintenance blackout Elena / Tom — Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. To summarize the agreed path so we have a single source of truth before Legal and Procurement finalize redlines: 1) Uptime & credits: Redwood to propose Order Form language with 99.99% Tier A, stepped credit schedule as proposed by Hannah, monthly cap 12%, annual cumulative cap 25%. 2) Response ladders & RCAs: P1 ack 1 hour / initial mitigation 4 hours; RCA within 72 hours, remediation plan within 10 business days. 3) Maintenance: Blue Harbor blackout for reconciliation (first Sunday 02:00–06:00 local) will be honored; scheduled maintenance limited to 8 hours/quarter plus up to 24 hours/year outside those buckets unless mutually agreed; 30 days' notice for non-emergency maintenance. 4) Operational mitigations: Redwood commits to phase 1 (KV priming) at Go-Live, and to a 90-day rollout plan for canary fallback (phase 2). Testing window of 30 days to validate fallback behavior. 5) Legal: Hannah will circulate a tracked redline of the Order Form and MSA incorporating the above. Procurement (Blue Harbor) to review; target DocuSign by 2025-09-18 if redline is accepted. Attachments included: BlueHarbor_MSA_redline.docx, SLO_matrix_v3.xlsx, Maintenance_Blackout_Proposal.pdf Please reply with any corrections; otherwise let us know when Procurement has a preferred time for a 30-minute redline review with Legal (Hannah) and Ops (Jonas). Best, Vivek Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
